title: Investigating Algorithmic Stock Market Trading using Ensemble Machine Learning Methods

data_binding.reason: shared benchmark data replaces the paper's native dataset and protocol

requirements: Daily stock market data sufficient to compute technical indicators
Stock high, low, and close prices for volatility-related calculations
SPY data as the market benchmark approximation
BIL data as the risk-free-rate approximation

dimensions.implication: The benchmark uses a frozen shared dataset rather than the paper's original data.
Only an explicitly named MethodCard model branch may enter the benchmark.
Shared features isolate model behavior but do not reproduce the paper's end-to-end pipeline.

paper_value.evaluation: Run the trained algorithm in the Quantopian simulator day-by-day over a time period greater than two years with fixed starting capital of 1,000,000 US dollars; assess performance at the end of the simulation using Quantopian-style trading performance indicators.

dimensions.implication: The shared temporal split and metric definitions control comparability across methods.

dimensions.paper_value: {"commission": "$0.03 per share", "slippage": "Quantopian default slippage model; orders limited to up to 2.5% of total available stocks"}
dimensions.implication: Trading claims require matched cost and position rules; prediction-only metrics do not establish tradability.

paper_vs_run_delta.original_paper_hypothesis_reason: Shared benchmark data/features/splits differ from the native paper protocol; the original claim cannot be proved or disproved by this run.
paper_vs_run_delta.adapted_task_hypothesis_reason: The benchmark result does not provide sufficient skill evidence on this frozen task.
